title: Practice Exam 3
description: A third full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam. Challenging level.

questions.question: There is no posted speed limit on a residential street near a park. The speed limit you must assume is:
choices: 25 mph
30 mph
35 mph
20 mph
questions.explanation: When no sign is posted, the default limit in a residential or business district is 25 mph. Always slow further for pedestrians, parked cars, and children near parks.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limits

questions.question: You must turn your headlights on:
choices: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and whenever you can't see 1,000 feet ahead
Only after it is completely dark
Only between midnight and 5 a.m.
Only on unlit roads
questions.explanation: Headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, and any time visibility drops below 1,000 feet. You must also turn them on whenever your wipers are in continuous use.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — When to Use Headlights

questions.question: A white rectangular sign with black lettering is a:
choices: Regulatory sign stating a law you must obey
Warning of a hazard ahead
Guide sign giving directions or distances
Construction sign
questions.explanation: White regulatory signs (speed limit, no U-turn, one way) state laws. Yellow diamonds warn; orange means construction; green guide signs give directions.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Regulatory Signs

questions.question: You approach a flashing red light at an intersection where the cross street has a flashing yellow light. You must:
choices: Stop, then proceed when safe; cross traffic may slow but need not stop
Slow down without stopping
Proceed first because you arrived
Treat it as a green light
questions.explanation: Flashing red = stop (like a stop sign). Flashing yellow = slow and proceed with caution. The cross street with the yellow does not have to stop, so you must yield to it after stopping.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Flashing Signals

questions.question: You are leaving a parking lot and crossing a sidewalk to reach the street. You must yield to:
choices: Pedestrians on the sidewalk and vehicles on the street
Only vehicles on the street
No one, since you are already moving
Only pedestrians directly in front of you
questions.explanation: When entering a road from a driveway, alley, or lot, you must yield to pedestrians on the sidewalk and to all traffic on the roadway before proceeding.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Entering Traffic

questions.question: Four cars reach a four-way stop. You stopped third. A pedestrian is also waiting to cross your exit. When it is your turn, you must:
choices: Proceed in your order, but still yield to the pedestrian crossing your path
Go ahead of the pedestrian since it is your turn
Wait for all other cars before going, ignoring order
Go before the pedestrian if you signal
questions.explanation: Vehicles proceed in arrival order at a four-way stop, but pedestrians in or entering a crosswalk always have the right of way over turning or crossing vehicles.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Four-Way Stops / Pedestrians

questions.question: Changing lanes while passing through an intersection is unsafe mainly because:
choices: Turning and cross traffic don't expect it, increasing collision risk
It is physically impossible to steer there
Your signals stop working in intersections
It always results in an automatic ticket
questions.explanation: Drivers turning into or crossing the intersection don't anticipate a lane change, so it's a high-risk move. Complete lane changes before or after the intersection.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Changing Lanes Safely

questions.question: A two-way center lane bordered by a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line on each side may be used:
choices: Only to begin or complete a left turn (or a legal U-turn)
As an extra travel lane in heavy traffic
To pass slower vehicles
For parking when spaces are full
questions.explanation: The center left-turn lane is shared by both directions and is only for preparing to turn left. Don't travel in it for more than about 200 feet or use it to pass.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Center Left-Turn Lanes

questions.question: At about 55 mph on dry pavement, the distance to perceive a hazard, react, and brake to a stop is closest to:
choices: The length of a football field (about 300 feet) or more
About one car length
About 50 feet
About 20 feet
questions.explanation: At highway speed the combined perception, reaction, and braking distance is on the order of a football field. This is why tailgating at speed is so dangerous.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Stopping Distances

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you closely on the highway. The safest response is to:
choices: Increase the gap to the car ahead and let the tailgater pass when you can
Tap your brakes to send a message
Speed up far above the limit to outrun them
Move left into the fast lane and slow down
questions.explanation: Open more space ahead so you can brake gradually, and let the tailgater go by when safe (move right). Brake-checking or speeding up only raises the danger.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Being Followed Too Closely

questions.question: Which is a realistic consequence of a FIRST DUI conviction in California?
choices: License suspension, fines, DUI program, and possible jail
A verbal warning only
No penalty for a first offense
Loss of license only if a crash occurred
questions.explanation: Even a first DUI can bring license suspension, substantial fines, mandatory DUI education, higher insurance, and possible jail time. Penalties escalate with repeat offenses.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — DUI Penalties

questions.question: An open, half-full bottle of wine sits in the back seat while a sober driver drives. This is:
choices: Illegal—open containers must be stored in the trunk or outside the passenger area
Legal because the driver is sober
Legal because it is in the back, not the front
Legal as long as the cap is on
questions.explanation: California's open-container law bans open alcohol in the passenger compartment regardless of who is or isn't drinking. Store it in the trunk or a locked area not in reach.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Open Container Law

questions.question: A crossing guard steps into the street and holds up a stop sign while your traffic light is green. You must:
choices: Obey the crossing guard and stop
Follow the green light and proceed
Proceed slowly around the children
Stop only if children are already crossing
questions.explanation: Directions from a crossing guard (or police officer) override traffic signals. Stop and wait until the guard signals you to go.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Crossing Guards

questions.question: Why must you be especially cautious driving near schools and parks?
choices: Children may dart into the street suddenly and not judge traffic well
The speed limit is always 15 mph there
Children always use the crosswalks
Traffic signals are turned off near schools
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable, may chase a ball or friend into the road, and often misjudge vehicle speed. Slow down and scan constantly in these areas.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving Near Schools

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left in an intersection when an ambulance approaches with siren on. You should:
choices: Clear the intersection if you can, then pull right and stop
Stop and wait where you are in the intersection
Complete a fast left turn directly in front of it
Reverse out of the intersection
questions.explanation: Don't freeze in the intersection. Move out of it safely, then pull to the right and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: A police officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the signal shows green for you, but the officer waves for you to stop. You must:
choices: Stop—an officer's directions override traffic signals and signs
Follow the green light
Choose whichever seems safer
Stop only if the officer blows a whistle
questions.explanation: Instructions from a police officer always take priority over signals and signs. Obey the officer even when it contradicts the light.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Obeying Officers

questions.question: Right turns are a frequent collision point with vulnerable road users. Before turning right you should most carefully check for:
choices: Bicyclists going straight on your right and pedestrians in the crosswalk
Only vehicles behind you
Only oncoming left-turning cars
Traffic two lanes to your left
questions.explanation: A right turn can cut across a cyclist continuing straight ('right hook') or a pedestrian stepping into the crosswalk. Check both before and during the turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Turning and Vulnerable Users

questions.question: On a roadway without a bike lane, a bicyclist is riding near the center of a narrow lane. This is:
choices: Legal—when a lane is too narrow to share, a cyclist may take the full lane
Illegal—cyclists must always hug the right edge
Illegal—cyclists must use the sidewalk
Legal only if the cyclist is a child
questions.explanation: When a lane is too narrow to share safely, a bicyclist may legally 'take the lane.' Slow down and pass only when you can give at least 3 feet.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: A curb is painted green. This means:
choices: Parking is permitted for a limited time shown by sign or marking
No parking at any time
Loading zone for freight only
Reserved for disabled parking
questions.explanation: Green curbs allow limited-time parking. Red = no stopping; yellow = loading; white = brief passenger loading; blue = disabled.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Colored Curbs

questions.question: Which location is it ILLEGAL to park in?
choices: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant
20 feet from a fire hydrant
In a marked space facing the correct direction
Parallel and within 18 inches of the curb
questions.explanation: You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Other illegal spots include crosswalks, intersections, sidewalks, and in front of driveways.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Where You May Not Park

questions.question: Your front tire suddenly blows out at freeway speed. You should FIRST:
choices: Grip the wheel firmly and ease off the gas to slow gradually
Brake hard immediately to stop fast
Accelerate to stabilize the car
Jerk the wheel toward the shoulder
questions.explanation: In a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, take your foot off the accelerator, and let the car slow before easing onto the shoulder. Hard braking or sudden steering can cause a spin.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Handling Emergencies

questions.question: Your engine dies and you coast to a stop on the freeway. The safest thing to do is:
choices: Get as far onto the right shoulder as possible, turn on hazard lights, and stay aware of traffic
Stay in the travel lane with hazards on and wait for help
Stand behind the car in the lane to warn traffic
Walk across the lanes to the call box on the far side
questions.explanation: Get well onto the shoulder, switch on hazard lights, and if you must exit, leave from the side away from traffic. Never stop in a live lane or stand in traffic.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Freeway Breakdowns

questions.question: Hands-free phone calls are legal for adults, yet still risky mainly because:
choices: They cause 'inattention blindness'—your mind misses hazards even with eyes forward
They are actually illegal for everyone
Holding the wheel with one hand is the only problem
They drain the car battery
questions.explanation: Even hands-free conversation splits your attention so you can look at a hazard without truly seeing it. The safest choice is to pull over for important calls.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Cognitive Distraction

questions.question: The best time to set your navigation destination and choose your music is:
choices: Before you start driving, while parked
At each red light along the way
While driving slowly in the right lane
While stopped in slow traffic
questions.explanation: Program devices before you move. Doing it at lights or in traffic still pulls your attention from the road and the cars around you.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Avoiding Distractions

questions.question: A steady red traffic light at a standard intersection means:
choices: Stop and remain stopped, except you may turn right after stopping if not prohibited
Stop, then go when you feel it is clear
Slow down and yield without stopping
Stop only if cross traffic is present
questions.explanation: A steady red means a full stop and wait for green. The only movement allowed is a right turn (or left from a one-way onto a one-way) after stopping, where not prohibited.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: A red ARROW pointing right is displayed for your turn lane. You may:
choices: Not turn right until the signal changes—unlike a red ball, a red arrow forbids the turn
Turn right after a complete stop, as with a red ball
Turn right if pedestrians are absent
Turn right whenever traffic is clear
questions.explanation: A red arrow prohibits movement in that direction until it changes; you cannot treat it like a red ball that allows a right turn after stopping.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Signal Arrows

questions.question: To turn right at a corner, you should position your car:
choices: As close as practical to the right curb or in the right-turn lane before turning
In the center of the road to swing wide
In the left portion of the lane
Anywhere in the lane, as long as you signal
questions.explanation: Move close to the right edge or into the right-turn lane before turning, and end in the nearest right lane. Swinging wide invites cyclists and cars to slip up your right side.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Making Turns

questions.question: Flashing red lights and a lowering gate at a railroad crossing mean:
choices: Stop and wait; do not cross until the lights stop and the gate is fully up
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers
Drive around the gate if no train is visible
Proceed slowly with caution
questions.explanation: Flashing reds and a gate mean a train is coming. Stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the gate rises completely—never drive around a gate.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Railroad Crossings

questions.question: You begin to skid on a wet road and the rear of the car slides to the right. You should:
choices: Ease off the gas and steer to the right, in the direction you want the front to go
Brake hard and hold the wheel straight
Steer left, against the skid
Accelerate to pull out of it
questions.explanation: In a skid, take your foot off the accelerator (don't slam the brakes) and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. Sudden braking or counter-steering worsens it.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Skids

questions.question: You park facing uphill on a street that has NO curb. Turn the front wheels:
choices: Toward the edge of the road, so a backward roll takes the car off the road
Away from the edge of the road
Toward the center line
Straight, and use only the parking brake
questions.explanation: With no curb (uphill or downhill), point the wheels toward the road's edge so a runaway car rolls away from traffic. A curb only changes the uphill case.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: You are driving with high beams on a dark highway and a car appears coming the other way. You must switch to low beams before you are within:
choices: 500 feet of the oncoming car
300 feet of the oncoming car
150 feet of the oncoming car
1,000 feet of the oncoming car
questions.explanation: Dim your high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle (and within 300 feet when following one). High beams blind other drivers and reduce everyone's safety.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Using Your Headlights

questions.question: Driving in steady rain after a dry spell can be most slippery:
choices: During the first several minutes, as rain lifts oil and grime to the surface
Only after several hours of heavy rain
Only when the rain has stopped
Never—rain has little effect on traction
questions.explanation: Roads are often most slippery just after rain begins, when water mixes with built-up oil and dust. Slow down and increase following distance.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving in the Rain

questions.question: A driver who has used cannabis (marijuana) and feels 'okay to drive':
choices: Can still be impaired and charged with DUI; cannabis slows reaction and judgment
Is safe because cannabis is legal for adults
Is only at risk of a ticket, not a DUI
Is fine if they drive below the speed limit
questions.explanation: Driving while impaired by cannabis is a DUI, just like alcohol. Legal status doesn't change the impairment to coordination, reaction time, and judgment.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Cannabis and Driving

questions.question: At a crosswalk a pedestrian has stepped off the far curb and is two lanes away from you, crossing toward you. You should:
choices: Yield and remain stopped until they are safely past your side of the road
Proceed because they are still far away
Proceed if you can clear the crosswalk before they reach your lane
Wave them to hurry and then go
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk until they have safely passed your lane. Trying to beat them or waving them on can lead to a collision if they stop or change pace.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pedestrians

questions.question: You need to exit the freeway two exits ahead during moderate traffic. You should:
choices: Move right one lane at a time early, then slow down on the off-ramp
Stay in the left lane until the exit, then cross all lanes
Slow down now in the through lane to be ready
Speed up to pass everyone before merging right
questions.explanation: Plan ahead and move right one lane at a time, signaling each move. Keep your speed up until you're on the deceleration ramp, then slow—don't brake in the through lanes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Exiting the Freeway

questions.question: Before any lane change, the single most important check is to:
choices: Confirm the target lane is clear, including a shoulder check of the blind spot
Make sure your speed is higher than traffic
Confirm your mirrors are clean
Sound your horn to warn others
questions.explanation: Signal and check mirrors, but the decisive step is making sure the lane—blind spot included—is actually clear before you move. A shoulder check catches what mirrors miss.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Safe Lane Changes
